class SharedRunState:
    """Container for the mutable per-run state shared across threads within a
    single script run.

    Holds the widget/form/fragment tracking sets and the command telemetry
    state. A script run may spawn helper threads (e.g. parallel fragments) that
    all read and write this state concurrently, so every field is guarded: the
    tracking sets are ``ThreadSafeSet`` instances, and the command telemetry is
    protected by an internal lock.

    ``track_command`` and read an immutable snapshot via the ``tracked_commands``
    property, which prevents downstream consumers from mutating the shared list.
    """

        self.widget_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.widget_user_keys_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.form_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.new_fragment_ids: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()

        # can't lose commands via a racing check-then-append.

        self._tracked_commands_counter: collections.Counter[str] = (
            collections.Counter()

    @property
    def tracked_commands(self) -> tuple[Command, ...]:
        """An immutable snapshot of the commands tracked so far.

        Returns a tuple (``()`` when empty) rather than the underlying list, so
        downstream consumers cannot mutate the shared telemetry state.
        """
        with self._command_lock:
            return tuple(self._tracked_commands)

    @property
    def tracked_commands_count(self) -> int:

        is not the same as the raw number of tracking calls.

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import threading
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.thread_safe_set import ThreadSafeSet

class SharedRunState:
    """Container for the mutable per-run state shared across threads within a
    single script run.

    Holds the widget/form/fragment tracking sets and the command telemetry
    state. A script run may spawn helper threads (e.g. parallel fragments) that
    all read and write this state concurrently, so every field is guarded: the
    tracking sets are ``ThreadSafeSet`` instances, and the command telemetry is
    protected by an internal lock.

    The tracked-command list is never exposed directly. Callers append through
    ``track_command`` and read an immutable snapshot via the ``tracked_commands``
    property, which prevents downstream consumers from mutating the shared list.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.widget_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.widget_user_keys_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.form_ids_this_run: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()
        self.new_fragment_ids: ThreadSafeSet[str] = ThreadSafeSet()

        # Guards the command telemetry state below so concurrent worker threads
        # can't lose commands via a racing check-then-append.
        self._command_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._tracked_commands: list[Command] = []
        self._tracked_commands_counter: collections.Counter[str] = (
            collections.Counter()
        )

    @property
    def tracked_commands(self) -> tuple[Command, ...]:
        """An immutable snapshot of the commands tracked so far.

        Returns a tuple (``()`` when empty) rather than the underlying list, so
        downstream consumers cannot mutate the shared telemetry state.
        """
        with self._command_lock:
            return tuple(self._tracked_commands)

    @property
    def tracked_commands_count(self) -> int:
        """The number of commands currently stored in the tracked list.

        This is bounded by the per-command cap passed to ``track_command``; it
        is not the same as the raw number of tracking calls.
        """
        with self._command_lock:
            return len(self._tracked_commands)

    def track_command(self, command: Command, max_per_command: int) -> None:
        """Track a command, capping how many of each name are stored.

        The command is appended to the tracked list only if a command with the
        same name has been tracked fewer than ``max_per_command`` times. The raw
        per-name counter is always incremented, regardless of the cap, so
        ``command_count_for`` reflects every call.

            if self._tracked_commands_counter[command.name] < max_per_command:
                self._tracked_commands.append(command)
            self._tracked_commands_counter.update([command.name])

        with self._command_lock:
            return self._tracked_commands_counter[name]

        self.widget_user_keys_this_run.clear()
        self.form_ids_this_run.clear()
        self.new_fragment_ids.clear()
